problem: Fuglede's conjecture on whether nonconvex sets in R and R2 are spectral if and only if they tile by translation
missing_details: The set Ω⊂ℝ^d must be measurable, bounded, and have positive finite Lebesgue measure
Definition of spectral set: existence of a countable spectrum Λ⊂ℝ^d such that {e^{2πi⟨λ,x⟩}:λ∈Λ} is an orthogonal basis of L^2(Ω)
Definition of translational tile: existence of a discrete set T⊂ℝ^d with ⋃_{t∈T}(Ω+t)=ℝ^d up to measure zero and (Ω+t)∩(Ω+t') has measure zero for t≠t'
Clarification that d is exactly 1 or 2
Explicit roles of Λ (spectrum) and T (tiling complement)
The orthogonality and completeness conditions in L^2(Ω)
refined_question: Let d be 1 or 2. Let Ω⊂ℝ^d be a bounded, Lebesgue‐measurable set of positive finite measure. We say that Ω is spectral if there exists a countable set Λ⊂ℝ^d such that the exponential functions {e^{2πi⟨λ,x⟩}:λ∈Λ} form an orthogonal basis of L^2(Ω). We say that Ω tiles ℝ^d by translations if there exists a discrete set T⊂ℝ^d such that the union of translates ⋃_{t∈T}(Ω+t) equals ℝ^d up to a null set and the translates are pairwise disjoint up to measure zero. Is it true that Ω is spectral if and only if Ω tiles ℝ^d by translations?
justification: The original conjecture (Fuglede, 1974) asserts the equivalence of spectrality and translational tiling for every domain Ω⊂ℝ^d (d arbitrary) ([en.wikipedia.org](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fuglede%27s_conjecture)). Partial results show the conjecture is resolved negatively for d≥3 and remains open precisely for d=1,2 ([en.wikipedia.org](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fuglede%27s_conjecture)). The refined formulation restricts to the open cases d=1,2 and includes all necessary definitions and hypotheses (boundedness, measurability, positivity and finiteness of Lebesgue measure, definitions of spectrum and tiling) that are implicit in the general statement but missing from the problem name.
